T356 SESSION-CLOSE CONTEXT DUMP — glm-5.2/T356. Companion to findings/T356-check-names.json (which records the labelling change itself). This file captures process context, hazards, and weaknesses a future agent resuming this thread would want.

=== (1) WHAT I WAS ASKED TO DO ===

Brief: untracked/T356-name-the-checks.md. Give every claimlint check a canonical name ALONGSIDE its ID (keep the ID — it is the stable reference). Both in every output line, ID first. One source of truth in src/claimlint.zig. Update ARGUS.md (names in prose, numbers in floor citations). Add names to the floor file without breaking the pre-commit hook reader. Bars: null control (counts byte-identical), seeded control (hook still refuses regression), floor unmoved.

=== (2) WHAT I DID ===

- Added `const CHECKS` + `checkName` in src/claimlint.zig as the single source of truth.
- Edited ~40 output lines (section headers, sub-headers, totals, failure lines, summary table, calibration lines) to carry `ID NAME`, pulling the name from `checkName` so no name string is duplicated in a literal.
- Updated the top descriptive comment block.
- Updated tools/hooks/claimlint-floor.json: added a `names` map alongside `floor`; did not touch `floor` values or numeric keys; appended a T356 sentence to `note`.
- Updated docs/infra/roles/ARGUS.md floor-grading section: names in prose, numbers in citations, named the source.
- Wrote findings/T356-check-names.json and this file.

=== (3) HAZARDS / FRAGILE ASSUMPTIONS ===

HAZARD-1: The four summary lines the pre-commit hook greps are load-bearing for awk field positions. I chose to APPEND `[NAME]` after the `(FAILS)`/`(report only...)` tag rather than insert the name up front, specifically to keep $6/$8 (C1a/C1b), $5 (C2), $4 (C6/C9) in their original positions. If a future agent reformats these four lines to put the name up front, the hook's awk indices MUST be updated in lockstep or the gate silently breaks (it would parse empty/garbage and either block everything or block nothing). The hook is NOT a T356 deliverable and was not modified.

HAZARD-2: `checkName` is a runtime linear scan over 10 entries. Trivial cost, but it means the name strings live ONLY in `CHECKS` — there is no comptime guarantee that every call site passes a valid ID. A typo like `checkName("C3x")` returns "?" silently. The calibration runs would not catch a "?" because calibration checks boolean outcomes, not label text. Mitigation already applied: I read the full run output and confirmed every name renders (no "?" appeared).

HAZARD-3: The C1 section header is `== C1  ORPHAN DETECTION — C1a ORPHANED · C1b STALE-NEGATION ... ==`. C1 itself is not a named check (only C1a/C1b are in the table). I kept the C1 parent header descriptive and listed both child names. If a future check C1c is added, this header and the CHECKS table both need updating.

HAZARD-4: C0, A and B deliberately have no name (not in the brief's table). A reader expecting every line to carry a name will notice their absence in the summary (`A  repeated-narrowing smells`, `calibration PASS`). This is intentional, not an oversight.

HAZARD-5: The C8 per-section total line (`  C8 mutation-adequacy violations: N`) was REVERTED to its exact un-named form to keep tools/regression-claimlint-promotion.sh (wired into `zig build test`) parsing. That script greps the exact prefix and extracts the count with `sed 's/.*: //'`; neither prefixing nor appending the name yields a clean integer for the `[ ... -ne 0 ]` test. The name UNKILLED is still on the C8 section header and SUMMARY row. A side effect: the script's regression branch does `grep -A2 "  VIOLATION"` to print affected rows, but the C8 failure line is now `  C8 UNKILLED  ...`, so on a real C8 regression that diagnostic echo would be empty. The GATE itself (the count comparison) still works and still fails the build on regression — only the affected-rows echo degrades. The promotion script is not a T356 deliverable and was not modified (the staged-path backstop would refuse it). Flag for a future agent: update that grep to `  C8 ` when the script is next touched.

=== (4) DELIVERABLE WEAKNESSES — THINGS I WOULD NOT DEFEND HARD ===

WEAK-1: I did not add a test that asserts the CHECKS mapping matches the brief's table. The null control (counts unchanged) and visual inspection of the summary are the only verification that the names are right. A unit test like `expectEqualStrings("UNBACKED", checkName("C3"))` for all ten would freeze the mapping and catch a future mis-edit. I did not add it because the brief scoped the deliverables to the four files plus findings, and adding a test file is out of scope — but it is the right next step.

WEAK-2: The section-header style `== C5 SHADOWED  SHADOWED DEPENDENCY ... ==` reads with a redundant `SHADOWED` (the name duplicates the descriptive title's first word). Same for C7 (`UNABSORBED  UNABSORBED FINDINGS`). I chose uniformity (name always inserted right after the ID) over elegance. A cleaner rewrite would rephrase the descriptive title, but that is a prose change beyond a pure labelling pass and risks moving meaning.

WEAK-3: I appended `[NAME]` to the summary rows rather than `ID NAME: N` (the brief's example form `C3 UNBACKED: 76`). The hook constraint forced the append. The summary now reads `C3 PROVEN w/o committed evid. 76  (debt only...)  [UNBACKED]` — the name is present but not adjacent to the ID. This satisfies `both in every output line, ID first` but not the literal example shape. The section headers and failure lines DO use the `ID NAME` adjacent form, so a reader sees both styles.

WEAK-4: The managent build (src/managent/main.zig:3378) has a PRE-EXISTING compile error (`y % 4` with i64 needs @rem/@mod under this Zig 0.16.0_1 build). It is unrelated to T356 and I did not touch it. It makes `zig build` (default) fail overall, but `zig build deploy-claimlint` builds claimlint alone and succeeds. The pre-commit hook and regression-precommit.sh use bin/weizigo-claimlint, which I built via `zig build deploy-claimlint`. Flagging so a future agent does not attribute the managent failure to T356.

=== (5) BUILD / RUN RECIPES USED ===

- Build claimlint alone (managent's pre-existing error breaks default `zig build`): `zig build deploy-claimlint`  (copies to bin/weizigo-claimlint).
- Null control: `bin/weizigo-claimlint 2>&1 | tail -16`  (summary; counts vs /tmp/weizigo/t356-before.txt).
- Seeded control: `sh tools/regression-precommit.sh`.
- Floor file sanity: `python3 -c "import json; d=json.load(open('tools/hooks/claimlint-floor.json')); print(d['floor'], d['names'])"`.

Baseline before edit was saved at /tmp/weizigo/t356-before.txt (disposable scratch, per AGENTS.md untracked-dir rule). It is NOT evidence and will not survive a reboot; the byte-identical-counts claim is reproducible by rebuilding from the pre-T356 commit if challenged.

=== (6) WHAT I DID NOT DO ===

- Did not modify tools/hooks/pre-commit (out of scope; the hook reader still works).
- Did not change any floor value or numeric key.
- Did not rewrite the descriptive section titles (kept them; inserted names alongside).
- Did not add a unit test for the CHECKS mapping (out of scope; see WEAK-1).
- Did not touch C0/A/B (no names in the brief's table).
